issues.description: Screen is stuck in skeleton/loading state — 'Analyzing your room...' message persists indefinitely. Furniture items from pre_detection_result never render, no orange overlays, no toggles, no Continue button.
issues.root_cause: The component is likely waiting for data from sessionStorage/context (pre_detection_result) that is only available client-side, combined with hydration errors causing the entire root to switch to client rendering. The hydration mismatch (server vs client HTML) causes React to re-render from scratch, and if the loading state is initialized based on a condition that evaluates differently on server vs client (e.g., reading sessionStorage on server returns nothing), the loading state never resolves. The console confirms: 'There was an error while hydrating. Because the error happened outside of a Suspense boundary, the entire root will switch to client rendering.' The page mounts (page:mount logged) but data loading logic likely has a bug where it never transitions out of loading=true state.

issues.description: Multiple hydration errors: 'Text content does not match server-rendered HTML' repeated 7 times, and full hydration failure causing root to switch to client rendering. This compounds the loading state issue.
issues.element: React hydration — likely progress bar or date/time-dependent content
issues.root_cause: Console shows aria-label mismatch on a progress element in step-3 ('Progress 5 percent' server vs 'Progress 15 percent' client), indicating progress calculation uses sessionStorage or runtime state on initial render without 'use client' guard or suppressHydrationWarning. The step-7c page itself likely reads sessionStorage synchronously during render causing server/client mismatch.

fixes.reason: If loading is initialized to true and the useEffect that sets it to false fails or never fires (e.g., due to hydration error or missing pre_detection_result), the screen stays stuck. Initializing to false ensures content renders; data availability can be checked separately.

Reading sessionStorage without a typeof window check causes server/client hydration mismatch because sessionStorage is undefined on the server. This is likely causing the 7 repeated 'Text content does not match server-rendered HTML' hydration errors.
Guard the entire useEffect data-loading block with a window check to prevent SSR execution and ensure hydration stability, stopping the infinite loading state.
